Feature universe for both model pipelines built from the 88 leakage-free ORIGINATION_FEATURES. Dropped zip_code (about 900 levels, impractical to bin) and the raw earliest_cr_line date string, and added a derived numeric cr_hist_yrs (credit-history length in years = interval from earliest_cr_line to issue date). Final universe 87 features. LightGBM uses all 87 with the 11 character columns as factors and missing kept native; the WOE-logistic pipeline screens this set further by Information Value.

Weight-of-Evidence bins and Information Values were estimated on the fit set only (2012 to 2013-H1, 106741 loans) and then applied unchanged to calib and test via woebin_ply, which maps values onto pre-learned bins without re-estimating them. No information from the calibration or test eras enters the feature transformation. This is the central leakage-safety guarantee of the protocol (Contribution 1).

Candidate features screened by Information Value at the standard scorecard threshold IV >= 0.02 (the conventional floor for weak-but-usable predictors), retaining 28 of 67 binned features for the WOE-logistic scorecard. The cut falls between num_actv_rev_tl (IV 0.022, retained) and tot_cur_bal (IV 0.018, dropped).

Strongest predictors by IV: sub_grade 0.323, int_rate 0.320, grade 0.316, then term 0.144 and the two FICO bands at 0.113 each. No feature exceeds IV 0.5 and the maximum is only moderate. This flat, leakage-free IV profile is itself evidence that the origination-only feature set is clean, unlike leaky LC studies where a single outcome-encoding field dominates. Two modelling notes for A6: (a) fico_range_low and fico_range_high are perfectly collinear (high = low + 4), both at IV 0.113, so only one enters the scorecard; (b) the grade/sub_grade/int_rate trio encodes one LC-assigned risk construct (sub_grade is the fine grade, int_rate near-deterministic in it), to be handled via with-versus-without LC-risk-view scorecard variants rather than entered together.

20 candidate features are entirely constant within the 2012 to 2013-H1 fit window and were dropped automatically at the binning step. They are the joint-applicant fields (annual_inc_joint, dti_joint, verification_status_joint, revol_bal_joint, application_type), the installment-account bureau block (open_acc_6m, open_act_il, open_il_12m, open_il_24m, mths_since_rcnt_il, total_bal_il, il_util, open_rv_12m, open_rv_24m, max_bal_bc, all_util, inq_fi, total_cu_tl, inq_last_12m), and disbursement_method. All were added to the Lending Club schema after about 2013, so they carry no variation in the early fit era. Direct evidence of feature-schema drift across the credit cycle; feeds the Chapter 5 results and Chapter 6 discussion drift narrative.
